extracted.intended_audience: university researchers, research administrators, faculty development staff, and program evaluators interested in grant-writing support
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation of an 8-month grant-writing group for social scientists aimed at increasing proposal submissions and funding success; describes program design elements (workshop format, peer review, coaching) and outcome measures (submission counts, funding success rates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program goal: increase applications and successes
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal was to increase applications and successes in funding competitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the primary objective guiding the group's design and evaluation; outcomes are measured against this goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer "homegrown" workshops that are ongoing rather than occasional
rubrics_metrics.description: Offering "homegrown" workshops that were ongoing rather than occasional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Porter (2011b)-informed strategy: locally run, sustained workshops are perceived to encourage more and better grant proposals compared with one-off events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share successful proposals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing examples of successful applications helps attendees understand standards and expectations; the article notes this as a beneficial component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide coaching and editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Coaching and editing support for proposal drafts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active editing and personalized coaching were integrated into the group to improve proposal quality and readiness for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bring together emerging and established researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Bringing together emerging researchers with established ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mixing career stages is intended to facilitate mentoring, model successful practices, and leverage experience to help less-experienced applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place participants in reviewers' shoes
rubrics_metrics.description: Placing participants in reviewers' shoes (peer review exercises).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Having participants review proposals as if they were funder reviewers helps them understand review criteria and improve their own submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured monthly sessions that require drafting each proposal section
rubrics_metrics.description: A series of monthly sessions that required participants to write each section of a grant proposal and share it with others for feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stepwise, time-boxed approach (one section per session) creates momentum and produces concrete, reviewable writing for peer and coach feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer feedback, accountability, and community-building
rubrics_metrics.description: The approach provided useful feedback and examples, and developed a sense of accountability and community among participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community and accountability are highlighted as mechanisms that increase commitment to submitting proposals; perceived by participants as working well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome metric: number of applications submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of applications submitted for funding as an evaluation metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this program evaluation the number of applications submitted increased 80% from the funding cycle just prior to the group to the cycle during/immediately after the group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome metric: success rate of funding (proportion funded)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate of success in obtaining funds from internal and external grant submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured success rate increased from 33% to 50% over the same time period in the evaluation; success rate is used to assess program effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differential impact: greater benefits for emerging/alternative academics
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest increase in submissions and success were experienced by emerging and alternative academic researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program appears especially effective for researchers with limited prior experience in funding competitions; design/targeting considerations should account for audience.
